newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee trade wants incentives for growers.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee trade wants incentives for growers.

text.p: Ugandan coffee traders have called for special incentives for traders and growers to boost production and exports.
Traders in Kampala urged the government to make credit readily available to farmers for fertilisers and insecticides.
They said farmer efforts were severely hampered by a lack of finance for smallholders due to very high interest rates on loans from commercial banks.
Smallholders also complained about larger growers.
"The major problem we are facing today in the coffee industry is that due to the competition in the market, the big players are taking over all the trade and we are not protected," one said.
The Uganda Coffee Development Authority sees exports falling to 3.6 million 60-kg bags in 1996/97 from a record 4.15 million bags in 1995/96 and earnings to $296 million from $389 million.

It forecast exports at 674,080 bags in the first quarter of 1996/97 (Oct/Dec) with earnings at $55 million, compared with 795,502 bags worth $88 million in the same quarter of the previous crop year. --Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261
